body: # Why Did Medtronic Stock Fall Despite Beating Q3 Earnings. Medtronic's Q3 FY26 earnings report presented a classic "beat and drop" scenario, with shares initially rising **2.9%** in pre-market trading before ultimately falling **4.7%** to **$94.85** following the announcement. The market's focus quickly shifted from the impressive revenue and adjusted EPS figures to underlying concerns about profitability and the nuances of the company's reaffirmed, rather than raised, full-year guidance. The medical device giant delivered its strongest enterprise revenue growth in **10 quarters**, reporting **$9.02 billion** in worldwide revenues, an **8.7%** year-over-year increase on a reported basis, and **6.0%** organically. Investors often interpret a stock's decline after an earnings beat as a sign that the "quality" of the beat was insufficient, or that the forward outlook failed to inspire confidence. This was driven by a **7%** increase in research and development (R&D) expenses to **$722 million** and an **8.8%** jump in selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses to **$2.96 billion**.
